notes.title: July Dev Log
notes.notes:
[p]Hey folks! We’ve been hard at work since announcing the game, and wanted to show off some of our progress. Let’s take a peek![/p][p][/p][p][i]Note: Some material such as ability icons or skill text may be WIP or missing final assets.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645323/3a6556055f763aaf6f6f216c4b643659e021485c.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]First up is the reveal of the final two playable character classes for the game; the Pod Person and the Detergilist! The Pod Person can spawn a clone of herself that mirrors her movements and attacks things in its path for a limited amount of turns.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645323/f1fadd924b7598b9132e17218e6096882d329521.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645323/380f2a58969e127768c32aa3e1682fad8b4094c5.png"][/img][/p][p]If you prefer to let your fists do the talking, the Detergilist may [i]look[/i] chill, but his Crystal Crash lets him barrel through enemies for short distances, doing damage [i]and[/i] getting out of tight spots.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645323/5d0bcbd1c5a99dd968fb52e5dfd1cab95fdcdaf0.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645323/d9717f98d622291684a8e9b8505ef7a680348689.png"][/img]
[/p][p]All of these classes also have access to a whole slew of different perks that can be selected when you level up between stages. The options you’re given are drawn from a pool of random upgrades that range from simple boosts to stats like health, to more complex abilities that will let you jump farther or equip multiple weapons at once. [/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfsjO-Wzqo2wfaGDj4LOM_n078PubreG1P22Qs8WNcLFGLoYotEtBG47ISD-cOPGxsJyj22QbihxaPwpeDmoJg52jGtUIgHPAO95S3DQQ8BLb9a-cHlwlXVVg12nbCV188ScMzw3Q?key=1hK23JhD1lLGrJ0tFTqxSw"][/img][/p][p]We’re also working on more enemies for the game, which involves a fair amount of iteration. Take a look at the Bug Bear’s sketch vs final sprite. There’s a fair amount of creepy-cute in Scrubbin’ Trubbles roster of Nasties, and we think the Bug Bear definitely leans more towards the latter. Please don’t try and hug him if you value all your limbs.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645323/543ea27bb674a97c9509e8e6ebbb2705fcb6a064.png"][/img][/p][p]We’ve also done a lot of work this month on general gameplay balancing and mechanics. We’re working on making each stage a little more dangerous by including traps that can snare you [i]and[/i] enemies, as well as having some [i]lasting consequences[/i] for individual runs if you let the overall grime in the house reach a certain threshold. While Scrubbin’ Trubble is designed for shorter play sessions compared to some roguelikes, we want to ensure it still has the variety and challenge players expect from the genre.[/p][p][/p][p]We’ll go into that and more next time, but for now, thank you for your support, and don’t forget to wishlist us if you haven’t already![/p]

notes.title: Announcing: Scrubbin' Trubble!
notes.notes:
We here at Odd Object would like to introduce you to our first game: [b]Scrubbin' Trubble[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45645323/644c34022915d56120d16a68fd055ee48c496dc7.png[/img]

Scrubbin' Trubble is a traditional, turn-based roguelike where you and your buddies play as miniature [i]Cleaning Agents[/i] tasked with cleaning up The House. As you traverse the kitchen, bathroom, living room, and other spaces in The House, you'll take on roaches, slimes, dust bunnies, and all kinds of other Nasties, tidying up as you go! You'll be able to play with up to 3 friends as you level up and eventually face down the Four Filths of the Apocalypse.

[h3]You..."and your buddies"?![/h3]

Yup, that's right! A basic characteristic of classic roguelikes is that they're completely turn-based: When you move, the world moves. Everything is synchronized in lock-step. This is straightforward for single-player games, but with ST we're trying something unique to allow multiple players to engage in the same play space simultaneously without forcing a global turn lock or limiting turns with a timer to keep the action.

[h3]A shorter dev cycle[/h3]

Scrubbin' Trubble's lead designer, Tyriq, has most recently come up for breath from a series of games with particularly long development times; he worked on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1147860/UFO_50/]UFO 50[/url] for six years, and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/315840/Catacomb_Kids/]Catacomb Kids[/url] is now over a decade old (and still underway!). When we started Scrubbin' Trubble, we knew we wanted to keep it smaller in scope than those games, so it's a simpler and shorter game than we're used to making, but with no less quality or passion put into it.

In game development, spending less time on a project can be harder than spending an indeterminate amount of time. But this commitment is a much needed change of pace for us, and we expect it to be more sustainable in the long run. We're stoked to be able to create and share more games more quickly.

Excited to share more details soon -- see you in the filth!
